title: Converting an advantage: take, exchange or stay quiet
outcomes: Lists the kinds of move available when clearly ahead: take material, exchange pieces, make a threat, make a quiet move
Asks what the opponent's best reply would be before taking a pawn
Chooses among the kinds in positions the engine rates as clearly better, and names what the engine's line shows
Does not treat 'clearly ahead' as a reason to stop calculating

steps.text: When you are clearly ahead, the advantage has to be turned into something that cannot slip away. Your kinds of move: **take material**, **exchange pieces**, **make a threat** (a pawn push or piece move that attacks something), or play a truly **quiet move** that keeps his counterplay small. Before you choose, ask: after my move, what is his best reply? The strongest move is not always the one that wins the most.

steps.caption: White to move and clearly ahead. The rook can take the pawn on b7.

line.say: The rook takes the pawn and attacks the queen and the bishop.

claims.statement: The engine rates the position at least 300 centipawns in White's favour.
After Rxb7 the rook attacks a7 and e7.
Rxb7 is the engine's best move.
Qxb7 is at least 300 centipawns worse than Rxb7.

steps.text: Which kind of move is best depends on the position, so this is a *rule of thumb* and not a recipe. Taking is often best when the capture is also the strongest line. An exchange can be best when it leaves an ending you can judge. A threat can be best when it forces a concession. A quiet move can be best when a capture would give him counterplay. Being clearly ahead still needs moves: check his forcing replies first.

steps.title: Take, threaten, wait or trade
steps.prompt: The engine rates all three positions as clearly better for the side to move. Predict which kind of move is best in each, then check.

Think of a game of yours where you were clearly ahead and the win slipped. Which kind of move (take, exchange, threaten or quiet) did you play, and what was your opponent's best reply at the moment you chose? Write the move and the reply.
